questions.q: What do you get back if RETURNING lists objects without any field lists, such as RETURNING Account, Contact, Lead?
options: Only the record Ids of the matching records
Nothing; the statement is invalid
Only the Name field of each record
Every field of every matching record
questions.explain: To get useful columns you put a field list in parentheses after each object, such as Account(Id, Name, Industry).

questions.q: Where do WHERE, ORDER BY and LIMIT go when you want to shape one object's SOSL results?
options: In a separate SELECT statement
They cannot be used in SOSL
After FIND, applying to every object
Inside that object's parentheses in RETURNING, applying to that object only
questions.explain: Per-object WHERE, ORDER BY and LIMIT go inside each object's parentheses, for example Account(Id, Name WHERE Industry = 'Technology' ORDER BY Name LIMIT 10).

questions.q: In Apex, how are the results of a multi-object SOSL search returned?
options: As a single Account list
As a map keyed by search term
As one flat list with all objects mixed together
As a list of lists, one per object, in RETURNING order
questions.explain: Apex returns List<List<SObject>>. The first list holds the first object named in RETURNING, and so on.

questions.q: Which SOSL fragment returns only Leads that have not been converted?
options: Lead WHERE IsConverted = false (Id, Name)
Lead(Id, Name WHERE IsConverted = false)
FIND {Lead} WHERE IsConverted = false
Lead(Id, Name) WHERE IsConverted = false
questions.explain: The WHERE goes inside the object's parentheses, after the field list.

questions.q: Which is a common mistake with multi-object SOSL results?
options: Forgetting to add a FROM clause
Getting too few columns because SELECT * was not used
Using braces around the search term
Expecting one combined table, when each object's results are separate with their own columns
questions.explain: SOSL results are grouped per object with different columns. SOSL has no FROM, and braces around the term are required in the standard form.
